title: START: Scalable Tracking for any Rowhammer Threshold
problem: Rowhammer attack thresholds have decreased from 139K to 4.8K activations, causing the number of possible aggressor rows to increase inversely. Existing defenses either require prohibitively high storage overheads (hundreds of KBs to MBs) or sacrifice guaranteed protection through approximate tracking.
motivation: As Rowhammer thresholds continue to decrease, practical defenses must provide scalable, secure, and storage-efficient tracking mechanisms to protect DRAM systems.
method: START protects against Rowhammer attacks by tracking frequently-accessed memory rows, but reuses space in the Last-Level Cache (the CPU's largest data cache) instead of requiring dedicated hardware. It works because real workloads only access a fraction of memory rows in the 64-millisecond refresh window, so there's usually spare cache space available. The system dynamically allocates storage by repurposing 1-way, 2-way, or 8-way cache sets based on how much memory activity is happening, using just 9.4% of cache capacity on average. For large-memory systems, START-M extends this using memory-mapped metadata.
key_novelty: START repurposes the Last-Level Cache as demand-allocated storage for Rowhammer tracking metadata, eliminating dedicated hardware without sacrificing accurate protection.
contributions: START tracker that scales to arbitrarily low Rowhammer thresholds using dynamic LLC allocation
5x reduction in storage overhead compared to per-row counter approaches
START-M extension for large-memory systems with only 4KB of additional SRAM
Performance within 1% of idealized tracking even at thresholds below 100

metrics.area: 9.4% LLC on average (5x lower than per-row); 4KB additional SRAM
metrics.other: Performance within 1% of idealized tracking at T_RH < 100

primary_theme: Scalable Rowhammer defense via dynamic cache allocation
